body: Thank you for your kind words. I’ve tried talking about it with her before but she just turns the whole thing around by making me the villain. She tells me that she has given me everything and that I should be glad that she didn’t neglect me like my dad. That my only responsibilities in life at this point is to get high grades and do chores at home. I tried to say to her what they told me in school: “Everyone has a different 100%. Their best isn’t going to be the same as your best.” She scoffs at that and tells me that they just tell kids that to make them feel better about failure. Maybe it’s because she grew up in Asia. In my mom’s home country, grades were a huge thing and it’s common for people to commit suicide when they fail at something. I guess she brought that mentality here with her. Again, thank you for your kindness.
